note: One people, tradition or figure from history for every country in the Americas, the Caribbean included.

ABW.name: Dande singer
ABW.note: At New Year a band goes house to house and sings your luck for you.

AIA.name: Anguillian boat racer
AIA.note: The national sport is sailing wooden boats built on the beach.

ATG.name: Sailor of Nelson's Dockyard
ATG.note: A harbour hidden in a bay, where whole fleets were repaired.

BHS.name: Junkanoo dancer
BHS.note: Costumes of crêpe paper, goatskin drums, and a parade before dawn.

BLM.name: Saint-Barth straw weaver
BLM.note: Hats and baskets plaited from latania palm, and Norman bonnets.

BLZ.name: Garifuna
BLZ.note: Caribbean and African together, with drums that talk in threes.

BMU.name: Gombey dancer
BMU.note: Peacock feathers, mirrors, whistles and a snare drum through the streets.

BRB.name: Landship performer
BRB.note: A whole navy on dry land, marching and dancing as a ship.

CRI.name: Boyero
CRI.note: Oxcarts painted like flowers, each one with its own creak.

CUB.name: Son musician
CUB.note: A tres guitar, a bongo and a chorus, on a porch in Santiago.

CUW.name: Tambú drummer
CUW.note: A drum, a hoe blade for a bell, and songs that say what cannot be said.

CYM.name: Catboat builder
CYM.note: A small boat built for turtling, shaped entirely by eye.

DMA.name: Kalinago
DMA.note: The last territory of the Caribbean's first islanders, and their canoes.

DOM.name: Merengue dancer
DOM.note: An accordion, a two-headed drum, and feet that never stop.

GRD.name: Shortknee masquerader
GRD.note: Wire masks and powder thrown at carnival, in trousers cut short.

GUY.name: Makushi
GUY.note: People of the savanna between the forest and the mountains.

HND.name: Lenca potter
HND.note: Black-and-white pots, coiled by hand and fired in a garden.

HTI.name: Soldier of the Haitian Revolution
HTI.note: The enslaved rose, won, and made the first free Black republic.

JAM.name: Maroon
JAM.note: Free towns in the mountains, and an abeng horn to call between them.

KNA.name: Kittitian masquerade dancer
KNA.note: Peacock feathers and ribbons, dancing between Christmas and New Year.

LCA.name: La Rose society
LCA.note: Half the island is Rose, the other half Marguerite, and each has its feast.

MAF.name: Saint-Martin salt raker
MAF.note: Salt raked from the ponds by hand and carried out in baskets.

MSR.name: Montserrat masquerader
MSR.note: Irish and African at once, on an island with shamrocks and a volcano.

NIC.name: Güegüense dancer
NIC.note: A four-hundred-year-old play where the trickster wins by talking.

PAN.name: Guna
PAN.note: Molas: layer on layer of cloth cut away to make a picture.

PRI.name: Vejigante
PRI.note: A carnival demon in a horned mask made of papier-mâché.

SLV.name: Nahua-Pipil
SLV.note: The old people of these volcanoes, and their Nawat language.

SPM.name: Basque and Breton fisherman
SPM.note: A piece of France off Canada, settled by cod fishermen.

SXM.name: Ponum dancer
SXM.note: A dance that began as a celebration of emancipation.

TCA.name: Ripsaw musician
TCA.note: The rhythm is a knife scraped along a carpenter's handsaw.

TTO.name: Steelpan player
TTO.note: An oil drum beaten into the only new instrument of the last century.

VCT.name: Garifuna
VCT.note: Yurumein, the island where the Garifuna people began.

VGB.name: Tortola sloop sailor
VGB.note: Wooden sloops built on the beach and raced between the islands.

VIR.name: Quadrille dancer
VIR.note: A European square dance, taken over and given a new rhythm.

BRA.name: Kayapó
BRA.note: People of the Xingu, with headdresses like a yellow sunburst.

CHL.name: Mapuche
CHL.note: The people of the land, who were never conquered by Spain.

COL.name: Wayuu
COL.note: Desert people of La Guajira, and bags crocheted with their own signs.

ECU.name: Otavalo weaver
ECU.note: Weavers and traders whose market is famous across the continent.

FLK.name: Falklands shepherd
FLK.note: More sheep than people, and a long ride between the farms.

PRY.name: Ñandutí lace maker
PRY.note: Lace made in circles — the name means 'spider web'.

SUR.name: Maroon of the Suriname River
SUR.note: Villages upriver founded by people who freed themselves.

URY.name: Candombe drummer
URY.note: Three drums of three different sizes, walking down the street together.

VEN.name: Llanero
VEN.note: Cattlemen of the flooded plains, who sing to the herd at night.
